correctness.rationale: For each of 13,824 four-agent normalized preference profiles, and each of 36 three-agent and two two-agent normalized profiles, the embedded exact Python checker reconstructs all assignment majority margins and covering relations. Its complete nonnegative rational dual certificates prove covered assignments have zero mass in every mixed-popular lottery for McKelvey at four and all three refinements at smaller sizes. A house-permutation symmetry argument proves enumeration completeness. Both separately specified four-agent mixed-popular counterexamples are checked against all 24 pure opponents and against explicit covering witnesses. All checks passed; no extrapolation beyond four agents is asserted.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 majoritarian-assignment paper explicitly asks about the support of mixed-popular lotteries in the uncovered set, without resolving the exact up-to-four-agent McKelvey case or the sharp Bordes/Gillies separation. Classical essential-set containment for sign-only payoff tournaments does not imply magnitude-sensitive majority-margin inclusion. Prior research records on rank-maximality, probabilistic-serial welfare and classical uncovered tournaments make no matching implication. Full-text inspection was done for the motivating source and relevant portions of the classical exposition. Residual priority risk from unindexed results remains.

value.rationale: The result provides a sharp finite boundary for two natural stronger uncovered refinements, a positive result for the standard McKelvey set, and two explicit rational-lottery witnesses. It addresses a concrete support-set question explicitly motivated in recent majority-assignment research, not a mere arbitrary profile census. Complete exact integer dual certificates make the finite structural guarantee reproducible. It does not claim a general theorem beyond four agents.
